evidence: Complementary analytical techniques were employed to investigate the crystallinity (grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction), composition (Rutherford backscattering analysis/nuclear reaction analysis/X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy), morphology (X-ray reflectivity/atomic force microscopy) which revealed the formation of amorphous, homogeneous and nearly stoichiometric Ga2O3 thin films. The optical band gaps and refractive indices indicated the formation of the desired target material at low temperatures. The process was verified by in situ QCM studies and ex situ measurements. The thickness, as well as refractive index measurements, were additionally derived from SE. In situ QCM measurements were performed. Crystallinity of the films was determined via GI-XRD measurements. Thin film thickness on Si(100) was measured using XRR. AFM of selected samples was performed. Compositional analysis of thin films deposited on silicon was determined by RBS in combination with NRA. XPS was performed to investigate the chemical composition of the sample surface. UV-Vis spectroscopy of the samples deposited on quartz substrates was performed.
